gloss: to be short-handed; to not have enough help

definitions.gloss: to be short-handed; to lack enough people to do the work
definitions.explanation: For there not to be enough people available for the work at hand. Literally 'hands are insufficient' — {手|て} stands for working hands, as in English 'we're short-handed.'

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{手|て}が{足|た}りない。
{手|て}が{足|た}りないので、アルバイトを{増|ふ}やすことにした。
examples.english: We're short-handed, so we decided to take on more part-timers.

examples.japanese: {年末|ねんまつ}は{注文|ちゅうもん}が{増|ふ}えて、どうしても{手|て}が{足|た}りなくなる。
examples.english: Orders pick up at the end of the year, so we inevitably end up short-handed.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しの{当日|とうじつ}は{手|て}が{足|た}りないと{思|おも}うので、{友人|ゆうじん}にも{来|き}てもらう{予定|よてい}だ。
examples.english: I expect we'll be short-handed on moving day, so I'm planning to have friends come too.

notes:
STRUCTURE: {手|て} (hand, worker) + が + {足|た}りない (to be insufficient).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {手|て}が{足|た}りない: we're short-handed
- {手|て}が{足|た}りなくなる: to end up short-handed
- {人手|ひとで}が{足|た}りない: to be short of staff (the same idea with the noun {人手|ひとで}; slightly more formal, common in news writing)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {人手不足|ひとでぶそく}: labor shortage — the noun used for the long-term, industry-wide problem
- {猫|ねこ}の{手|て}も{借|か}りたい: so busy one would borrow a cat's paws — a vivid idiom for the same situation

USAGE:
Use it for a temporary shortfall on a particular day or job; a chronic shortage is {人手不足|ひとでぶそく}.
